name: TRUSS

intro.problem: Network architectures in physics analyses are usually chosen by convention, and little evidence says the default topology is right once a network must deliver background closure [@abcdisco2020][@cms2025tec] as well as discrimination.
intro.value: A statistically scored topology search, borrowed from generative structural design [@hahn2023][@nie2020], could find networks that keep their discriminating power while closing better, replacing architecture-by-habit with architecture-by-evidence.
intro.approach: TRUSS has two components. Testing existing: measure how much adding or removing connections moves the current networks, then relax that grid into learned GRU-style sigmoid gates on connection groups [@cho2014][@louizos2018]. Testing new: generate candidates from the trained models' latent features using gated blocks [@dauphin2017][@srivastava2015], growth [@evci2022] and evolution [@real2018]. Every candidate is trained supervised, and a surrogate fitted to those results makes the search itself supervised [@nie2020].
intro.goals: The deliverables are a calibrated connection sensitivity, a population of tested architectures retrained from scratch on seeds disjoint from the search [@zela2019], a random-search baseline beside every search, and a Pareto front of the real trade-offs.

questions: At what granularity do connection changes measurably move performance, and can learned gates find that structure faster than a grid?
Can the latent features of trained models seed architectures that beat the current default?
Can a supervised surrogate trained on our own results predict which untested architectures will close best?

components.name: Testing existing
components.subtitle: Optimize the current networks
components.summary: Start from the networks already in use and find out how sensitive they are to their own topology before inventing anything new. Every result here becomes the baseline the new designs must beat.

items.label: Connection calibration
items.detail: Drop or add connections in groups across the three baseline designs, in both detector regions, with every metric recorded

items.label: Learned gates
items.detail: GRU-style sigmoid gate on each connection group, relaxed to exactly open or closed [@louizos2018]; must match or beat the calibration grid

items.label: Closure-sensitivity pruning
items.detail: Remove units whose closure cost is high and whose classification value is low, from one backward pass

components.name: Testing new
components.subtitle: Generate and test new architectures
components.summary: Use the latent features of many trained models to propose architectures that have not been tried, then train and score each one. The inner loop is ordinary supervised training; the outer loop starts as black-box search and becomes supervised once a surrogate is fitted.

items.label: Gated blocks
items.detail: Gated linear units and highway layers in place of plain layers [@dauphin2017][@srivastava2015]; per-feature gates for variable selection [@lim2019]

items.label: Split latent
items.detail: One shared trunk whose latent dimensions are gated to either network, with the dependence penalty between the two blocks

items.label: Grow and evolve
items.detail: Gradient-guided growth [@evci2022], regularized evolution [@real2018], and differentiable search with its known failure modes guarded [@liu2018][@zela2019]

items.label: Supervised surrogate
items.detail: Regress the metric vector on architecture parameters plus latent fields, then let it propose the next candidates [@nie2020]

items.label: Guardrails
items.detail: Disjoint seeds, winners retrained from scratch, a random-search baseline, and gates against designs that win by default
